gaps.sentence: 'I'm exhausted,' she said. She said she ___ exhausted.
gaps.explanation: Present simple/progressive shifts to past in reported speech: am → was.

gaps.sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
The hijackers ___ to blow up the plane unless their demands were met.
gaps.explanation: A declared harmful action is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'Let's walk to the launch instead of driving,' he said. He ___ to the launch instead of driving.
gaps.explanation: 'Suggest' takes a gerund, never a to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'Please reconsider my application,' she wrote. She ___ them to reconsider her application.
gaps.explanation: A polite written request is reported with asked + object + to-infinitive.
